title: Website Design in DeKalb, Illinois: What NIU-Area Businesses Should Know

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a fictional college-town cafe connecting student and resident needs through one mobile website; not an actual DeKalb location.

figures.title: One website, two customer contexts
figures.summary: The guide distinguishes year-round local needs from campus-oriented searches.

items.label: Year-round residents
items.detail: Look for established local services, contact details, and service-area relevance.

items.label: Students near campus
items.detail: Use phones to find nearby food, appointments, and everyday businesses.

items.label: Shared requirements
items.detail: Both need readable mobile pages, clear service information, and an obvious next action.

figures.caption: An audience-planning comparison from the article, without estimating the size or behavior of either group.

figures.title: Connect the local information consistently
figures.summary: Each layer should describe the same real business and service area.

items.label: Business profile
items.detail: Maintain accurate categories, contact information, and photos.

items.label: Useful service pages
items.detail: Explain actual services and the areas served without city-name-only duplication.

items.label: Directory details
items.detail: Keep name, address, and phone consistent across public listings.

items.label: Page metadata and schema
items.detail: Use descriptive titles and appropriate structured information.

figures.caption: The local SEO foundations listed in this guide; they do not guarantee a search position.
